audit.summary: Archived assessment: Major. The specified Rees filtration need not be additive; Smooth-locus identification fails for constructed open set at positive complexity; Missing necessary toric binomial in Example 4.17
limitations: M25-0286-P1 — The specified Rees filtration need not be additive — Counterevidence: Using formal degree fixes the secondary inequality, and the specific corrected t^2 binomial vanishes exactly under the indicated substitution. That does not repair the independent nonadditivity example. No unstated restriction to homogeneous f occurs in the displayed set definition.

M25-0286-P2 — Smooth-locus identification fails for constructed open set at positive complexity — Counterevidence: The zero weight ensures effectiveness. Positive complexity (6-3=3) permits a nonsmooth image for a smooth Hamiltonian manifold. The smooth-toric-manifold theorem does not apply. A smaller invariant open set works in this example; that possibility does not validate the printed equality for the specified U.

M25-0286-P3 — Missing necessary toric binomial in Example 4.17 — Counterevidence: A localization or saturation interpretation would exclude points but is not the stated affine equality. The general lattice-count and area identities are exactly correct; the prior 49 finite checks were inspected and the symbolic identity independently recomputed.

M25-0286-P4 — Proper onto image does not guarantee all-time gradient flow — Counterevidence: This example is not proper into the full target and is excluded by (GH4)II. In the theorem application, (GH4)III saturation also prevents a fixed-moment trajectory from leaving its assigned subfamily. The appendix's location is not the reason for Minor.

M25-0286-P5 — Strong convexity criterion loses zero-weight exception — Counterevidence: The earlier nonnegative-zero-combination criterion correctly rejects the example. The later Lemma 4.10 proves zero is not a weight, so its properness application is not refuted.

proposition.claim:
Equation reference: eq:filtration. On p. 20, following (15), the paper defines \[
 A_{\leq k}=\{f\in A:e(v(f))\leq k\text{ or }f=0\}\] and calls these sets subspaces forming a filtration. The Rees algebra (16) and Proposition 4.5 then use that assertion. The choice of \(e\) is constrained by nonnegativity on the value semigroup and the finitely many comparisons associated with the chosen relation generators.

Proposition 6.10(iii), p. 39, identifies the image of the constructed open piece with the smooth locus of the corresponding moment image. The proof on p. 40 treats \(\Delta_Y\cap\sigma\) as smooth. No multiplicity-free hypothesis is imposed on \(Y\). The proof of Theorem 1.1 on p. 41 invokes Proposition 6.10 for its first and third assertions.
